title: Bear encounter (no contact)
recognize: A bear has seen you and is close: standing up, huffing, following you or charging, but has not touched anyone
A bear in or near your camp or your food
do_first: Stay calm. Talk to the bear in a low, calm voice so it knows you are a person, and slowly wave your arms.
Stand your ground. Do not run: a bear can run as fast as a racehorse.
Pick up small children straight away. Stay together as a group and make yourselves look as large as you can.
Keep your pack on, and never let the bear get to your food.
If the bear is not moving, back away slowly and sideways, keeping an eye on it. If it follows you, stop and hold your ground.
Leave the area or take a wide detour, and always leave the bear a way out.
do_not: Do not climb a tree: grizzlies and black bears both climb
Do not imitate bear sounds or make high-pitched squeals
Do not drop your pack or leave food for the bear
Never get between a mother and her cubs
escalate_when: The bear makes contact with anyone: see the bear attack card

title: Bear attack (kind of bear not known)
recognize: A bear has made contact: knocked someone down, biting or clawing
You do not know yet whether it is a grizzly or a black bear, or whether it came into a tent or stalked you
do_first: Keep your pack on: it protects your back.
Bear came into your tent, or followed you first: do not play dead. Fight back at its face with everything you have.
Grizzly or brown bear (shoulder hump, dished face): play dead. Lie on your stomach, hands behind your neck, legs spread, still until it leaves. Fight back only if it keeps attacking.
Black bear (no hump, straight face): do not play dead. Get to a car or building if you can; otherwise fight back, hitting its face and muzzle.
do_not: Do not play dead for a black bear, or for any bear that came into your tent or stalked you
escalate_when: Always: anyone injured by a bear needs medical care. Report the attack to park rangers or wildlife authorities.

ask_first.question: What kind of bear is it? A grizzly has a big shoulder hump and a dished face; a black bear has no hump and a straight face. Colour does not tell you.
ask_first.label: Kind of bear

ask_first.question: Did the bear come into your tent, or follow you before it attacked?

title: Grizzly or brown bear attack
recognize: A grizzly or brown bear (big shoulder hump, dished face, long claws) has made contact
Usually a surprise, or a mother with cubs: the bear is defending itself
do_first: Keep your pack on and play dead.
Lie flat on your stomach with your hands clasped behind your neck.
Spread your legs so the bear cannot easily roll you over.
Stay still and quiet until the bear leaves the area. Fighting back usually makes the attack worse.
If the attack continues anyway, fight back as hard as you can with whatever you have, hitting the bear in the face.
When the bear is gone, treat injuries (stop heavy bleeding first) and get medical help.
do_not: Do not fight back first: see whether playing dead stops the attack
Do not play dead if the bear came into your tent or stalked you: fight back
escalate_when: Always: anyone injured by a bear needs medical care. Report the attack to park rangers or wildlife authorities.

regions: Northern Rocky Mountains (Montana, Wyoming, Idaho, Washington)

ask_first.question: Did the bear come into your tent, or follow you before it attacked?
ask_first.label: Tent or stalking attack

title: Black bear attack
recognize: A black bear (no shoulder hump, straight face, shorter claws; the coat can be black, brown or cinnamon) has made contact
do_first: Do not play dead.
If you can, get to a secure place such as a car or building.
If you cannot escape, fight back with any object you have.
Aim your kicks and blows at the bear's face and muzzle.
When the bear is gone, treat injuries (stop heavy bleeding first) and get medical help.
do_not: Do not run unless you can reach a car or building
Do not climb a tree: black bears climb well
escalate_when: Always: anyone injured by a bear needs medical care. Report the attack to park rangers or wildlife authorities.

title: Bear attack in a tent, or after stalking
recognize: A bear attacked inside a tent or shelter
A bear followed or stalked someone and then attacked
Any kind of bear: this bear may be looking for food and see people as prey
do_first: Do not play dead. Fight back with everything you have, and get everyone else to help.
Hit and kick at the bear's face and muzzle with any object: rocks, sticks, poles, pans.
Keep fighting until the bear gives up and leaves.
When the bear is gone, treat injuries (stop heavy bleeding first) and get medical help.
escalate_when: Always: anyone injured by a bear needs medical care. This kind of attack is very rare and serious: report it to park rangers or wildlife authorities straight away.
